sanskrit: snigdhagambhīraghoṣeṇa syandanenopayān prabhuḥ ayodhyāṃ bharataḥ kṣipraṃ praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ
english: The lord Bharata of great renown quickly entered Ayodhyā riding in a chariot whose sound was deep and resonant.

sanskrit: biḍālolūkacaritām ālīnanaravāraṇām timirābhyāhatāṃ kālīm aprakāśāṃ niśām iva
english: He found it as a dark, lightless night, haunted by cats and owls, its people and elephants cowering — struck through with gloom.

sanskrit: rāhuśatroḥ priyāṃ patnīṃ śriyā prajvalitaprabhām graheṇābhyutthitenaikāṃ rohiṇīm iva pīḍitām
english: Like Rohiṇī, the beloved wife of the enemy of Rāhu — though radiant with splendor — oppressed and afflicted by a planet that had risen against her.

sanskrit: alpoṣṇakṣubdhasalilāṃ gharmottaptavihaṃgamām līnamīnajhaṣagrāhāṃ kṛśāṃ girinadīm iva
english: Like a mountain river grown lean — its waters warm and turbid, its birds tormented by the summer heat, its fish and crocodiles sunk low.

sanskrit: vidhūmām iva hemābhām adhvarāgnisamutthitām havirabhyukṣitāṃ paścāc chikhāṃ vipralayaṃ gatām
english: Like a golden flame, smokeless, that had risen from a sacrificial fire, anointed with oblation, and then subsided into extinction.

sanskrit: vidhvastakavacāṃ rugṇagajavājirathadhvajām hatapravīrām āpannāṃ camūm iva mahāhave
english: Like an army in great battle that has lost its armor, its elephants, horses, chariots, and banners shattered, its foremost heroes slain.

sanskrit: saphenāṃ sasvanāṃ bhūtvā sāgarasya samutthitām praśāntamārutoddhūtāṃ jalormim iva niḥsvanām
english: Like a wave of the ocean that had arisen foaming and roaring, then fallen silent — the wind that stirred it now stilled.

sanskrit: tyaktāṃ yajñāyudhaiḥ sarvair abhirūpaiś ca yājakaiḥ sutyākāle vinirvṛtte vediṃ gataravām iva
english: Like a sacrificial altar grown silent after the soma-pressing is complete, abandoned by all the ritual implements and the handsome officiating priests.

sanskrit: goṣṭhamadhye sthitām ārtām acarantīṃ navaṃ tṛṇam govṛṣeṇa parityaktāṃ gavāṃ patnīm ivotsukām
english: Like a leading cow standing distressed in the middle of the cowpen, no longer grazing fresh grass, yearning — abandoned by the bull.

sanskrit: prabhākarālaiḥ susnigdhaiḥ prajvaladbhir ivottamaiḥ viyuktāṃ maṇibhir jātyair navāṃ muktāvalīm iva
english: Like a fresh pearl necklace bereft of its lustrous gems — those excellent, radiant stones with their lovely, captivating gleam.

sanskrit: sahasā calitāṃ sthānān mahīṃ puṇyakṣayād gatām saṃhṛtadyutivistārāṃ tārām iva divaś cyutām
english: Like a star that has suddenly left its place and fallen from the sky upon the exhaustion of its merit — its brilliance and expanse contracted.

sanskrit: puṣpanaddhāṃ vasantānte mattabhramaraśālinīm drutadāvāgnivipluṣṭāṃ klāntāṃ vanalatām iva
english: Like a forest creeper that at the end of spring was decked in flowers and humming with intoxicated bees, then scorched and wilted by a swiftly spreading forest fire.

sanskrit: saṃmūḍhanigamāṃ sarvāṃ saṃkṣiptavipaṇāpaṇām pracchannaśaśinakṣatrāṃ dyām ivāmbudharair vṛtām
english: Like a sky veiled by rain-clouds — its moon and stars hidden — with all its merchant quarters bewildered and every market and shop shut down.

sanskrit: kṣīṇapānottamair bhinnaiḥ śarāvair abhisaṃvṛtām hataśauṇḍām ivākāśe pānabhūmim asaṃskṛtām
english: Like a drinking hall in the open air, fallen into ruin — its finest wines exhausted, littered with broken vessels, its revelry slain, uncleaned.

sanskrit: vṛkṇabhūmitalāṃ nimnāṃ vṛkṇapātraiḥ samāvṛtām upayuktodakāṃ bhagnāṃ prapāṃ nipatitām iva
english: Like a watering station that has fallen and collapsed — its floor broken and sunken, covered with shattered vessels, its water fully used up.

sanskrit: vipulāṃ vitatāṃ caiva yuktapāśāṃ tarasvinām bhūmau bāṇair viniṣkṛttāṃ patitāṃ jyām ivāyudhāt
english: Like a bowstring — broad, extended, fitted with its cord for the swift archer — cut through by arrows and fallen from the weapon to the ground.

sanskrit: sahasā yuddhaśauṇḍena hayāroheṇa vāhitām nikṣiptabhāṇḍām utsṛṣṭāṃ kiśorīm iva durbalām
english: Like a young filly, weak, ridden suddenly by a battle-fierce horseman, then dropped and abandoned — her load cast aside.

sanskrit: prāvṛṣi pravigāḍhāyāṃ praviṣṭasyābhra maṇḍalam pracchannāṃ nīlajīmūtair bhāskarasya prabhām iva
english: Like the light of the sun hidden in the deep of the rainy season, its disc entered by rain-clouds, concealed by dark-blue storm clouds.

sanskrit: bharatas tu rathasthaḥ sañ śrīmān daśarathātmajaḥ vāhayantaṃ rathaśreṣṭhaṃ sārathiṃ vākyam abravīt
english: But Bharata, the glorious son of Daśaratha, seated in his chariot, spoke these words to the charioteer who was driving the finest of chariots.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalv adya gambhīro mūrchito na niśamyate yathāpuram ayodhyāyāṃ gītavāditraniḥsvanaḥ
english: "Why indeed is the deep, resounding noise of song and music that Ayodhyā used to have no longer heard today as before?"

sanskrit: vāruṇīmadagandhāś ca mālyagandhaś ca mūrchitaḥ dhūpitāgarugandhaś ca na pravāti samantataḥ
english: "The heady fragrance of wine, the rich scent of garlands, and the perfume of burned aguru incense — none of these waft in any direction."

sanskrit: yānapravaraghoṣaś ca snigdhaś ca hayaniḥsvanaḥ pramattagajanādaś ca mahāṃś ca rathaniḥsvanaḥ nedānīṃ śrūyate puryām asyāṃ rāme vivāsite
english: "The sound of the finest vehicles, the smooth neigh of horses, the trumpeting of lordly elephants in rut, the great rumble of chariots — none of this is now heard in this city, since Rāma has been exiled."

sanskrit: taruṇaiś cāru veṣaiś ca narair unnatagāmibhiḥ saṃpatadbhir ayodhyāyāṃ na vibhānti mahāpathāḥ
english: "The broad avenues of Ayodhyā no longer shine, graced by young men in elegant dress who walk with heads held high and move swiftly about."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jalpan viveśa vasatiṃ pituḥ tena hīnāṃ narendreṇa siṃhahīnāṃ guhām iva
english: Speaking thus in many ways, he entered his father's dwelling — bereft of that lord of men, like a mountain cave bereft of its lion.

sanskrit: tato nikṣipya mātṝḥ sa ayodhyāyāṃ dṛḍhavrataḥ bharataḥ śokasaṃtapto gurūn idam athābravīt
english: Then Bharata, firm in his vows and consumed by grief, having left the mothers in Ayodhyā, spoke these words to his elders.

sanskrit: nandigrāmaṃ gamiṣyāmi sarvān āmantraye 'dya vaḥ tatra duḥkham idaṃ sarvaṃ sahiṣye rāghavaṃ vinā
english: "I shall go to Nandigrāma. I take leave of all of you today. There I will endure all this sorrow without the son of Raghu."

sanskrit: gataś ca hi divaṃ rājā vanasthaś ca gurur mama rāmaṃ pratīkṣe rājyāya sa hi rājā mahāyaśāḥ
english: "For the king has gone to heaven, and my guru dwells in the forest. I wait for Rāma to return for the kingdom — he of great glory is the true king."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ abruvan mantriṇaḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaś ca purohitaḥ
english: Having heard this noble speech of the great-souled Bharata, all the ministers and the family priest Vasiṣṭha replied.

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ ślāghanīyaṃ ca yad uktaṃ bharata tvayā vacanaṃ bhrātṛvātsalyād anurūpaṃ tavaiva tat
english: "What you have spoken, Bharata, is fitting and praiseworthy — a word born of brotherly affection, suited to you alone."

sanskrit: nityaṃ te bandhulubdhasya tiṣṭhato bhrātṛsauhṛde āryamārgaṃ prapannasya nānumanyeta kaḥ pumān
english: "You are ever devoted to your kinsmen, steadfast in brotherly love, treading the path of the noble — what man would not approve of you?"

sanskrit: mantriṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā yathābhilaṣitaṃ priyam abravīt sārathiṃ vākyaṃ ratho me yujyatām iti
english: Having heard the agreeable and welcome words of the ministers, he spoke to his charioteer: "Let my chariot be yoked."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ sarvā mātṝḥ samabhivādya saḥ āruroha rathaṃ śrīmāñ śatrughnena samanvitaḥ
english: With a joyful countenance, he paid obeisance to all the mothers, and the glorious one mounted the chariot accompanied by Śatrughna.

sanskrit: āruhya tu rathaṃ śīghraṃ śatrughnabharatāv ubhau yayatuḥ paramaprītau vṛtau mantripurohitaiḥ
english: Having swiftly mounted the chariot, both Śatrughna and Bharata set out in great joy, surrounded by ministers and the family priest.

sanskrit: agrato puravas tatra vasiṣṭha pramukhā dvijāḥ prayayuḥ prāṅmukhāḥ sarve nandigrāmo yato 'bhavat
english: Ahead of the city, all the twice-born with Vasiṣṭha at their head proceeded facing east, toward where Nandigrāma lay.

sanskrit: balaṃ ca tad anāhūtaṃ gajāśvarathasaṃkulam prayayau bharate yāte sarve ca puravāsinaḥ
english: That army, dense with elephants, horses, and chariots, set out unbidden, and all the citizens of the city went forth as Bharata departed.

sanskrit: rathasthaḥ sa tu dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ nandigrāmaṃ yayau tūrṇaṃ śirasy ādhāya pāduke
english: That righteous-souled Bharata, devoted to his brother, seated in the chariot and bearing Rāma's sandals upon his head, quickly proceeded to Nandigrāma.

sanskrit: tatas tu bharataḥ kṣipraṃ nandigrāmaṃ praviśya saḥ avatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ gurūn idam uvāca ha
english: Then Bharata swiftly entered Nandigrāma, quickly descended from the chariot, and spoke these words to his elders.

sanskrit: etad rājyaṃ mama bhrātrā dattaṃ saṃnyāsavat svayam yogakṣemavahe ceme pāduke hemabhūṣite tam imaṃ pālayiṣyāmi rāghavāgamanaṃ prati
english: "This kingdom has been given to me by my brother himself as a trust. These golden-adorned sandals, which bear responsibility for welfare and protection, I will guard this kingdom in anticipation of the son of Raghu's return."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ saṃyojayitvā tu rāghavasya punaḥ svayam caraṇau tau tu rāmasya drakṣyāmi sahapādukau
english: "Quickly and by my own hand I shall place these sandals back upon the feet of the son of Raghu and behold Rāma's two feet together with his sandals."

sanskrit: tato nikṣiptabhāro 'haṃ rāghaveṇa samāgataḥ nivedya gurave rājyaṃ bhajiṣye guruvṛttitām
english: "Then, my burden set down, reunited with the son of Raghu, having rendered the kingdom to my guru, I shall take up the mode of life proper to a disciple."

sanskrit: rāghavāya ca saṃnyāsaṃ dattveme varapāduke rājyaṃ cedam ayodhyāṃ ca dhūtapāpo bhavāmi ca
english: "And having returned these excellent sandals and this kingdom and Ayodhyā itself as a trust to the son of Raghu, I shall be cleansed of sin."

sanskrit: abhiṣikte tu kākutsthe prahṛṣṭamudite jane prītir mama yaśaś caiva bhaved rājyāc caturguṇam
english: "When the scion of Kākutstha is consecrated and the people rejoice with delight, my happiness and my glory will be four times greater than a kingdom."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu vilapan dīno bharataḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ nandigrāme 'karod rājyaṃ duḥkhito mantribhiḥ saha
english: Thus lamenting, the wretched and grief-stricken Bharata of great renown administered the kingdom from Nandigrāma together with his ministers.

sanskrit: sa valkalajaṭādhārī muniveṣadharaḥ prabhuḥ nandigrāme 'vasad vīraḥ sasainyo bharatas tadā
english: The lord Bharata, that hero wearing bark garments and matted locks, clad in the guise of a sage, then resided in Nandigrāma together with his army.

sanskrit: rāmāgamanam ākāṅkṣan bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ bhrātur vacanakārī ca pratijñāpāragas tadā
english: Longing for Rāma's return, devoted to his brother, obedient to his brother's word, Bharata then fulfilled the vow he had taken.

sanskrit: pāduke tv abhiṣicyātha nandigrāme 'vasat tadā bharataḥ śāsanaṃ sarvaṃ pādukābhyāṃ nyavedayat
english: Having consecrated the sandals, Bharata then resided in Nandigrāma, referring all governance to those sandals.

sanskrit: pratiprayāte bharate vasan rāmas tapovane lakṣayām āsa sodvegam athautsukyaṃ tapasvinām
english: After Bharata had returned, Rāma, dwelling in the forest of austerities, began to perceive anxiety and agitation among the ascetics.

sanskrit: ye tatra citrakūṭasya purastāt tāpasāśrame rāmam āśritya niratās tān alakṣayad utsukān
english: Those ascetics who dwelt in the hermitage in front of Citrakūṭa, engaged in their practices and taking refuge with Rāma — he observed them to be restless.

sanskrit: nayanair bhṛkuṭībhiś ca rāmaṃ nirdiśya śaṅkitāḥ anyonyam upajalpantaḥ śanaiś cakrur mithaḥ kathāḥ
english: Pointing at Rāma with their eyes and with furrowed brows, anxious, they whispered to one another and exchanged hushed conversations among themselves.

sanskrit: teṣām autsukyam ālakṣya rāmas tv ātmani śaṅkitaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvācedam ṛṣiṃ kulapatiṃ tataḥ
english: Perceiving their restlessness, Rāma became anxious in his own heart, and with joined palms he then spoke to the seer, the master of the hermitage community.

sanskrit: na kaccid bhagavan kiṃ cit pūrvavṛttam idaṃ mayi dṛśyate vikṛtaṃ yena vikriyante tapasvinaḥ
english: "Blessed one, has something previously done by me been seen as a fault, by reason of which the ascetics are disturbed?"

sanskrit: pramādāc caritaṃ kaccit kiṃ cin nāvarajasya me lakṣmaṇasyarṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ nānurūpam ivātmanaḥ
english: "Has some act of my younger brother Lakṣmaṇa, done through carelessness, been seen by the seers as unbecoming of him?"

sanskrit: kaccic chuśrūṣamāṇā vaḥ śuśrūṣaṇaparā mayi pramadābhyucitāṃ vṛttiṃ sītā yuktaṃ na vartate
english: "Does Sītā, devoted to service toward me, who attends to you all, conduct herself with the behavior proper to a woman, as is fitting?"

sanskrit: atharṣir jarayā vṛddhas tapasā ca jarāṃ gataḥ vepamāna ivovāca rāmaṃ bhūtadayāparam
english: Then the seer, aged with old age and grown ancient through austerity, spoke as though trembling to Rāma, who surpasses all in compassion for living beings.

sanskrit: kutaḥ kalyāṇasattvāyāḥ kalyāṇābhirates tathā calanaṃ tāta vaidehyās tapasviṣu viśeṣataḥ
english: "How could there be any fault, dear one, in the daughter of Videha — she of auspicious nature and auspicious disposition — toward the ascetics especially?"

sanskrit: tvannimittam idaṃ tāvat tāpasān prati vartate rakṣobhyas tena saṃvignāḥ kathayanti mithaḥ kathāḥ
english: "This is happening to the ascetics on account of you — it is the rākṣasas. Terrified because of them, they whisper these tales to one another."

sanskrit: rāvaṇāvarajaḥ kaś cit kharo nāmeha rākṣasaḥ utpāṭya tāpasān sarvāñ janasthānaniketanān
english: "A certain rākṣasa named Khara, younger brother of Rāvaṇa, dwelling in Janasthāna, has been uprooting and harrying all the ascetics."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaś ca jitakāśī ca nṛśaṃsaḥ puruṣādakaḥ avaliptaś ca pāpaś ca tvāṃ ca tāta na mṛṣyate
english: "Insolent, boastful of his victories, cruel, a devourer of men, arrogant, and wicked — he does not, dear one, tolerate you."

sanskrit: tvaṃ yadā prabhṛti hy asminn āśrame tāta vartase tadā prabhṛti rakṣāṃsi viprakurvanti tāpasān
english: "From the very time that you, dear one, have been residing in this hermitage, from that time the rākṣasas have been harassing the ascetics."

sanskrit: darśayanti hi bībhatsaiḥ krūrair bhīṣaṇakair api nānā rūpair virūpair ca rūpair asukhadarśanaiḥ
english: "For they manifest themselves in loathsome, cruel, terrifying, and various hideous and misshapen forms that are painful to behold."

sanskrit: apraśastair aśucibhiḥ saṃprayojya ca tāpasān pratighnanty aparān kṣipram anāryāḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ
english: "Having defiled the ascetics with inauspicious and impure matter, those ignoble ones standing in front quickly strike down others."

sanskrit: teṣu teṣv āśramasthāneṣv abuddham avalīya ca ramante tāpasāṃs tatra nāśayanto 'lpacetasaḥ
english: "And those feeble-minded ones, hiding unseen in various hermitage sites, take delight in destroying the ascetics there."

sanskrit: apakṣipanti srugbhāṇḍān agnīn siñcanti vāriṇā kalaśāṃś ca pramṛdnanti havane samupasthite
english: "They hurl away the ritual ladles and vessels, douse the sacred fires with water, and crush the water-pots when the oblation rite is at hand."

sanskrit: tair durātmabhir āviṣṭān āśramān prajihāsavaḥ gamanāyānyadeśasya codayanty ṛṣayo 'dya mām
english: "Wishing to abandon these hermitages that have been overrun by those evil-souled ones, the seers are urging me today to depart to another region."

sanskrit: tat purā rāma śārīrām upahiṃsāṃ tapasviṣu darśayati hi duṣṭās te tyakṣyāma imam āśramam
english: "Before those wicked ones inflict bodily harm upon the ascetics, Rāma, we will abandon this hermitage."

sanskrit: bahumūlaphalaṃ citram avidūrād ito vanam purāṇāśramam evāhaṃ śrayiṣye sagaṇaḥ punaḥ
english: "There is a forest rich in roots and fruits, wondrous and not far from here; I will once again, together with my community, take refuge in that ancient hermitage."

sanskrit: kharas tvayy api cāyuktaṃ purā tāta pravartate sahāsmābhir ito gaccha yadi buddhiḥ pravartate
english: "Moreover, Khara perpetrates wrong against you yourself, dear one. Come away from here with us, if your mind so inclines."

sanskrit: sakalatrasya saṃdeho nityaṃ yat tasya rāghava samarthasyāpi hi sato vāso duḥkha ihādya te
english: "He who dwells with his wife is always beset by uncertainty, O scion of Raghu; even for one who is capable and virtuous, residence here is now painful."

sanskrit: ity uktavantaṃ rāmas taṃ rājaputras tapasvinam na śaśākottarair vākyair avaroddhuṃ samutsukam
english: The prince Rāma was unable to restrain with any words of reply that ascetic, who had spoken thus and was already eager to depart.

sanskrit: abhinandya samāpṛcchya samādhāya ca rāghavam sa jagāmāśramaṃ tyaktvā kulaiḥ kulapatiḥ saha
english: Welcoming Rāma, taking leave of him, and consoling the son of Raghu, the master of the hermitage community departed, abandoning the hermitage together with his groups.

sanskrit: rāmaḥ saṃsādhya tv ṛṣigaṇam anugamanād deśāt tasmāccit kulapatim abhivādyarṣim samyakprītais tair anumata upadiṣṭārthaḥ puṇyaṃ vāsāya svanilayam upasaṃpede
english: Rāma, having escorted the band of seers away from that region and dissuading the master of the hermitage community from following further, saluted the seer properly; approved by those joyful ones and instructed in his purpose, he proceeded to his own blessed dwelling to reside there.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ tv ṛṣivirahitaṃ prabhuḥ kṣaṇam api na jahau sa rāghavaḥ rāghavaṃ hi satatam anugatās tāpasāś carṣicaritadhṛtaguṇāḥ
english: The lord, that son of Raghu, did not abandon even for a moment the hermitage now deprived of its seers; for the ascetics, holding fast to the virtues proper to the conduct of seers, constantly followed after the son of Raghu.
